label: D2 after a rare a1->S2 transition while the policy still favors a1
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), and only when this trial chose a1 and reached S2, i.e. a rare transition after a1 (99.8% of mass; never after a2->S2 common or any S1 arrival). Within a1->S2R steps it is gated by the model policy logit at that step: active when logit(a1)-logit(a2) is above about 2.8 (a1 still preferred), so it fires mostly when S1 is good (86% of mass) and the agent keeps choosing a1. Magnitude is largest after an unrewarded previous trial (prev_reward==0 holds 93% of mass; activations after a rewarded previous trial are ~0.1-0.3 of max), with value in the mid range 5.2-7.5. Using prev_reward==0 instead of the choice threshold gives dev F1 0.66 (precision 0.92 and F1 0.80 if both are combined). All variables are observed at D2; choice is the model own policy readout, not a future variable. Does not fire at D1 or GO, on rewarded inputs, or on a2 trials.

issues: I reproduced the reported test scores exactly: P 0.758, R 0.921, F1 0.831, mass recall 0.984. Every activation is at D2 (D1 and GO have 0 active steps), and in_rew==1 has 0 active steps.

'Never fires after common a2->S2' is very slightly overstated. On dev, 48 active steps (0.2% of mass) have action==2 & state==2, and the predicate (phase==D2)&(action==2)&(state==2) has precision 0.0003. That is noise, not a counterexample class.
The choice threshold 2.78 is not optimal. With choice>3.0 test F1 is 0.856 (P 0.817, R 0.899, mass recall 0.978), and dev F1 rises from about 0.83 to 0.868. This is a refinement, not a refutation.

The remaining false positives (3418 test steps) cluster where the previous trial was rewarded. On dev, a1->S2 & prev_reward==1 & choice>2.78 has precision only 0.51 and holds 7% of the mass. This matches the explanation's point that the previous-reward effect is weaker, and the explanation already notes it.

The 'policy still favors a1' gate is the model's own D2 logit readout, not a clean task variable. Replacing it with observed history works much worse: prev_action==1 gives F1 0.38, and prev_reward==0 & prev_action==1 gives F1 0.58. So the gate depends on the internal policy state, as the label says. The label does not overclaim.
The test misses are scattered across rel positions and hold 1.6% of the mass. No systematic missed class was found.
